biological.citation: Lipophilic compounds restore function to neurodevelopmental-associated KCNQ3 mutations (PMID: 39300259)
biological.summary: Using voltage clamp fluorometry, molecular dynamic simulations, and electrophysiology, two distinct loss- and gain-of-function mechanisms were identified for NDD-associated KCNQ3 variants: one affecting S4 voltage-sensor movement and another affecting S4-to-pore coupling. Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) were shown to primarily target the voltage-sensing domain in its activated conformation, and two PUFA compounds yielded partial and complete functional restoration in R227Q- and R236C-containing KCNQ3 channels, respectively.

biological.citation: Electrophysiological Abnormalities and Pharmacological Corrections of Pathogenic Missense Variants in KCNQ3 (PMID: 40095209)
biological.summary: A library of 24 missense KCNQ3 mutations was introduced into three channel backgrounds (KCNQ3, KCNQ3-A315T, and KCNQ3-KCNQ2 tandem) and analyzed by patch-clamp recording. Loss-of-function mutations concentrated in the pore-forming domain were associated with self-limited familial neonatal epilepsy, while gain-of-function mutations (leftward V1/2 shifts) were associated with neurodevelopmental disorders; the KCNQ opener Pynegabine reversed LOF mutations and the KCNQ inhibitor Amitriptyline reversed GOF mutations including the novel G553R variant.

biological.citation: KCNQ2/3 Gain-of-Function Variants and Cell Excitability: Differential Effects in CA1 versus L2/3 Pyramidal Neurons (PMID: 37607817)
biological.summary: The R231C gain-of-function variant in KCNQ3 (homologous to R201C in KCNQ2) was expressed in transgenic mice and shown to cause hyperexcitability in layer 2/3 cortical pyramidal neurons but hypoexcitability specifically in superficial CA1 pyramidal neurons. These cell-type-specific effects reveal that KCNQ3 gain-of-function impacts neuronal excitability in a brain-region- and cell-type-dependent manner.

biological.citation: Donepezil as a new therapeutic potential in KCNQ2- and KCNQ3-related autism (PMID: 39175503)
biological.summary: In mouse primary cultured hippocampal neurons, 1 µM donepezil inhibited the M-current (mediated by KCNQ2/KCNQ3 channels) by 67% in excitatory neurons (IC50 ~0.4 µM) and increased spontaneous firing frequency 2.6-fold. In four children with gain-of-function KCNQ3 variants (p.Arg227Gln, p.Arg230Cys), off-label donepezil treatment for 12 months produced clinically significant improvement in autism symptoms in two patients.
biological.significance: p<0.05 for M-current inhibition in excitatory neurons

biological.citation: Increased KCNQ3 expression in papillary thyroid cancer promotes proliferation and migration (PMID: 41250218)
biological.summary: KCNQ3 was found to be aberrantly overexpressed in papillary thyroid cancer and mechanistically interacts with GAREM1, GRB2, and SOS1 (identified by co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry), activating the RAS/RAF/MAPK signaling cascade to promote tumor cell proliferation and migration. ChIP-qPCR revealed that estradiol (E2) enhances KCNQ3 transcription via estrogen receptor alpha (ESR1) binding to the KCNQ3 promoter, and the KCNQ channel inhibitor XE991 inhibited PTC cell proliferation and migration in vitro and in vivo.

biological.citation: DNA methylation and expression of KCNQ3 in bipolar disorder (PMID: 25041603)
biological.summary: In postmortem prefrontal cortex from bipolar disorder patients, KCNQ3 mRNA expression was significantly lower compared to matched controls, and DNA methylation at CpGs within KCNQ3 exon 11 was significantly reduced in BPD, correlating with KCNQ3 mRNA levels. Replication in the Stanley Medical Research Institute cohort confirmed lower KCNQ3 exon 11 methylation after correcting for mood stabilizer status, suggesting epigenetic dysregulation of KCNQ3 in BPD pathogenesis.
biological.sample_size: BPD cases and matched controls from McLean Hospital + Stanley Medical Research Institute cohort

biological.citation: Molecular and circuit determinants in the globus pallidus mediating control of cocaine-induced behavioral plasticity (PMID: 39153478)
biological.summary: In the globus pallidus externus (GPe), expression of KCNQ3 and KCNQ5 voltage-gated potassium channels was downregulated following cocaine exposure in parvalbumin-positive (GPePV) neurons, contributing to elevated GPePV cell excitability. Acute activation of KCNQ3/KCNQ5-containing channels with carnosic acid reduced GPePV excitability and impaired cocaine reward, sensitization, and volitional cocaine intake in mice.

biological.citation: Transcriptional control of KCNQ channel genes and the regulation of neuronal excitability (PMID: 20926649)
biological.summary: The transcription factor Sp1 activates KCNQ3 expression, while the transcriptional repressor REST represses KCNQ3 expression, establishing two key regulatory mechanisms controlling KCNQ3 mRNA levels. Transcriptional regulation of KCNQ3 was mirrored by correlated changes in M-current density and excitability in native sensory neurons, implicating these pathways in seizure activity and pain.

biological.citation: SMAD4 and KCNQ3 alterations are associated with lymph node metastases in oesophageal adenocarcinoma (PMID: 37648039)
biological.summary: Transcriptomic analysis of oesophageal adenocarcinoma identified KCNQ3 as associated with lymph node metastasis, with KCNQ3 uniquely linked to changes in planar cell polarity associated with non-canonical Wnt signaling (distinct from SMAD4's association with canonical Wnt). Overexpression of KCNQ3 in cell line and xenograft systems reduced wound closure and the number of metastases observed, suggesting a functional role in suppressing metastatic behavior.

biological.citation: KCNQ2 and KCNQ5 form heteromeric channels independent of KCNQ3 (PMID: 35320039)
biological.summary: Using split-intein protein trans-splicing to form KCNQ2/5 tandems and mass spectrometry of native brain channels, KCNQ2 was shown to associate with KCNQ5 in the brain even in the absence of KCNQ3, demonstrating that KCNQ channel composition is more diverse than the previously assumed KCNQ2/3 or KCNQ3/5 heteromers. Functional heterologous expression data were also consistent with the formation of KCNQ2/3/5 heteromers, necessitating re-examination of genotype/phenotype relationships for KCNQ3-containing channels.
